messages:
jia: Quick note — ran a targeted heat probe on AWQ weight-only packer yesterday. Observed consistent tail-latency spikes when KV cache was warm and group_size=64. Putting findings here so we have a short runbook for follow-ups.

mike: summary pls? numbers?

jia: TL;DR: throughput ~ same, p95 latency +18-24% on small-chat workloads (avg seq 64). Root cause looks like an extra memcpy path in the packer when alignment != slot_size that only triggers for group_size>=48 + hot KV hits.

ara: any kernel mismatches? selector logs?

jia: yes — kernel_selector flipped to `matmul_int8_unroll` for about 30% of batches (shorter sequences) and `matmul_int8_fused` for the rest. The problematic path happens when we fall back to the non-fused path and then hit the packer fixup; that adds ~0.6ms per token in our microbench.

sam: can you paste the mini profile?

jia: pasted below (sanitized):
```
SAMPLES: 1000
- KV lookup + hit: 12%
- packer_align_fixup (memcpy): 19%  <-- spike correlates with p95
- matmul_int8_unroll: 28%
- matmul_int8_fused: 35%
- others: 6%

p95_total: 42.1ms (baseline 34.9ms)
```

devon: what causes the align_fixup? buffer layout? quant alignment?

jia: it's the packer emitting per-group padding when group_size doesn't divide lanes. That padding path uses a slow scalar memcpy for the tail, whereas aligned groups go through the vector memcpy. Also prefetch logic does an extra check for KV hotness that seems to serialize with packer on the hot path.

mike: is this AWQ-specific or also seen with GPTQ?

jia: observed in both but AWQ amplifies it because group_size tends to be larger (48/64) and AWQ padding strategy differs. GPTQ default group 32 rarely hits the slow branch.

ara: perf regression after recent kernel selector tweak?

jia: yes — the selector change (PR #4521) started preferring unroll variant for short sequences which increased the chance to hit the packer fixup. Before PR we pretty much always used fused kernel for these models.

sam: suggested quick mitigations?

jia: 1) short-term: force fused kernel for seq>=32+AWQ models (cheap gate). 2) medium: change packer to use vectorized tail copy (needs careful bounds checks). 3) longer: update selector heuristic to include packer-cost estimate (profiled cost) instead of pure kernel throughput.

devon: can we experiment with 1) as a canary?

jia: yes — I pushed a branch that overrides kernel selection with a simple rule. Results on shadow-run: p95 dropped back to baseline, throughput unchanged. Shadow runs attached in the dump.

mike: great. Any tests to add so this doesn't regress again?

jia: add microbench for packer tail-case and a KV-hot synthetic workload that hits group_size boundary conditions. I'll open a tiny test harness PR.

ara: ops-bot, can we schedule a canary deploy to dedicated dev cluster? low risk config toggle.

ops-bot: deploy request received: job=canary/awq-kernel-override env=dev-dedicated id=canary-1739999999 status=queued

sam: one more observation — calibration step (calib pass post-quant) for AWQ is doing an extra memcpy-driven reserialize when group_size>=48; that adds ~0.3ms once per load and amplifies cold-starts. Worth fixing but lower priority.

mike: action items?

jia: ACTIONS:
- jia: open PR with kernel override + perf numbers (in review).
- jia: push microbench and KV-hot synthetic test (WIP).
- devon: prototype vectorized tail-copy for packer (help with correctness).
- ara: add regression alert for p95 delta > 12% on AWQ models in telemetry.
- ops-bot: run canary and report logs to #eng-ml-canary in ~1h.

sam: thanks — low-chatter sprint-friendly plan. ping if you need an extra hand on the patch. :thumbsup:

jia: I'll update the runbook with step-by-step debug commands and attach perf dumps. Quick debug commands for anyone trying to reproduce locally:
```bash
# run short shadow workload
PYTHONPATH=./svc python perf/run_shadow.py --model redwood/awq-v1 --group-size 64 --seq 64 --kv-hot 1 --iters 500

# collect selector traces
./bin/kernel_selector --trace sel.log --model-path foo.bin --seq 64 --group 64

# sample packer profile
perf record -e cycles:u -o perf.data ./bin/serving --lite-workload  --profile-pack=tail
```

devon: nice. leaving notes here so we don't lose the steps.

ops-bot: canary deployed: canary-1739999999 -> dev-dedicated (started). Logs: https://ci.redwood.internal/canary-1739999999

mike: keep this thread updated when canary finishes.

jia: will. thanks all.
